correctness.rationale: For odd m=n/2, row-minus-column parity descends to the twisted strip. A run's rainbow triangles are successive windows on the complementary track. For two nonadjacent empty columns the two windows lists are disjoint for two phase choices, giving 36 colourings each, and share exactly the two empty-column endpoints for the other two. Equality of endpoint colours is forced iff the separation is divisible by three on that list. Since 3 does not divide m, the lists cannot both force equality, and are compatible iff both separations are nonzero mod 3. The compatible shared case gives 54 per phase, including two free vertices. Adjacent empties give 108 per pair. There are m pairs per distance, giving 108m+72m(h-1)+108mg; reducing residues yields both quadratic laws, including m=5 with g=0. Weight m needs bipartiteness and the closed period-three sequence; with only one empty column an odd strip closes the two endpoints of the same track and again needs 3 dividing m. The even one-empty strip has distinct endpoints and recovers the credited linear case. Thus the revised proof also establishes the weights without importing a counting or existence assumption.

The independent code computes minima, unlike the supplied bounded checker, which is run at prescribed weights. Neither finite check proves the general case.
